newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan favors paying interest on bank reserves.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan favors paying interest on bank reserves.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday lent his support to a proposal to require that the U.S. central bank pay banks interest on reserve balances.

To avoid having to meet reserve requirements, banks are using a procedure called "retail sweeps" in which they move funds from traditional savings and checking accounts into money market deposit accounts, which are not subject to reserve requirements.
Fed reports on reserves have shown sharp declines as a result of the sweep accounts.

During the question-and-answer session of his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, Greenspan said paying interest on reserves would remove the incentive for creating such accounts and would bring the reserves, through which the Fed engineers changes in monetary policy, back into line.

"It would give us a greater control over monetary policy and it's an effective tool which, in my judgment, is something which, while not a major issue, is something ... I think would be helpful," the Fed chief told the Senate Banking Committee in the second part of his semiannual testimony to Congress.
Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato said in a statement that requiring the Fed to pay interest on the reserves would improve the efficiency of the financial system.
"We must remember, when banks aren't paid interest on these deposits, it's really bank customers who are potentially losing money," the New York Republican said.
